title: [RFC][Rollout] Support vLLM-RLT as a native rollout backend
body:
## Goal

Support vLLM-RLT as an optional rollout backend through VIME's standard `train.py` / `RolloutManager`, reusing Megatron training, reward/group handling, checkpointing and physical-weight conversion.

The first milestone is an Ouro GRPO loop with versioned generation, full policy publication and fresh-process resume. Keep the backend change small and independently reviewable.

## Existing work and dependencies

- [Ouro integration #459](https://github.com/vllm-project/vime/pull/459) is merged into `0z5a-branch`. It provides the shared-weight provider, recurrent replay, conversion and online engine interactions. Its legacy example manages its own engine; reuse that work when moving lifecycle ownership into the standard control plane.
- [Nanbeige #463](https://github.com/vllm-project/vime/pull/463) already contains a draft shared backend factory, native Ray engine, publication adapter and standard sample/trace integration. [Huginn #464](https://github.com/vllm-project/vime/pull/464) builds on it. This issue tracks backend acceptance and remaining lifecycle coverage alongside those PRs, without duplicating their model implementations.
- Coordinate the public score and weight-update contract with [vLLM-RLT #78](https://github.com/ThinkFlowLab/vllm-rlt/pull/78). The current integration pins [engine commit `d2a3589`](https://github.com/0z5a/vllm-rlt/tree/d2a358933393f25d74dd2bdd1068a741cd5d9226). Keep profile-specific score names and request/engine settings in one adapter. An accepted pinned companion can be documented as experimental; stable support requires an accepted upstream dependency.

Current staging base: [`0z5a-branch` at `3e56931`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vime/tree/3e569314a42a3de4aa99340021a4d00ad4e1f431). Draft implementation and legacy recipe results do not establish that the backend acceptance gate below has passed.

## Initial support contract

| Item | First milestone |
| --- | --- |
| Model / objective | Pinned Ouro-1.4B revision; standard online GRPO, no reference/critic/KL |
| Execution | Fixed full depth K=4; positive temperature and full-vocabulary sampling |
| Training layout | TP=PP=CP=1; DP only for explicitly validated world sizes |
| Resources | One native rollout engine with explicit trainer/rollout GPU ownership; initially separate resources |
| Updates | Full physical weights, initial actor publication and committed versions on outputs |
| Lifecycle | Start, ready/health, generate, drain/cancel, update, cooperative close and restart/republication |

Depth 2/3/4 and actual-depth replay regressions retain their own evidence. Colocation/offload, early exit, async generation, CUDA Graphs, PD/NIXL and speculation need separate capability and combination checks. Nanbeige/Huginn, PPO/DPPO/Flow-DPPO, RLTT and broader parallelism are follow-ups rather than prerequisites for the Ouro backend milestone.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Parse `--rollout-backend vllm-rlt` before engine-specific arguments; keep the default vLLM path and optional imports independent of RLT. Unsupported profiles/combinations fail before GPU allocation.
- [ ] Use a small factory and a Ray-owned engine adapter for startup, readiness, generation, request exclusion during updates, and cooperative teardown of this job's resources.
- [ ] Preserve standard `Sample` semantics for tokens, response length, mask, reward, group identity, behavior logprobs and weight versions. Carry a serializable recurrent trace with runtime epoch, committed policy identity, model/tokenizer/engine identities, execution plan, prefill and response-aligned actual depths, sampling/score settings, replay metadata and finish reason.
- [ ] Reuse physical-weight conversion: publish each shared block once, including required embeddings, norms, head and inference gates. Explicitly publish the actor's initial policy before accepting requests.
- [ ] Implement pause → drain/cancel → full manifest/chunks → validation → committed ACK → cache invalidation/version isolation → ready. Incomplete publication blocks generation until a full recovery; do not promise rollback of in-place copies. Same-version retries require the same manifest.
- [ ] Restore actor, optimizer, scheduler, RNG and rollout plan in a fresh process; create a new runtime epoch and republish the restored policy. Add resource release/recovery modes only when their engine contracts are verified.

## Acceptance gate

- [ ] Existing Ouro GRPO correctness is reproducible: shared parameters, score/depth alignment, at least two real optimizer updates, publication and checkpoint/resume.
- [ ] Standard `train.py` / `RolloutManager` runs without `debug-train-only`: v0 rollout → update/publish v1 → v1 rollout → update/publish v2.
- [ ] Default vLLM recipe passes with no RLT installation/import requirement.
- [ ] Mixed-length token/logprob/depth/version traces survive serialization, dump/load, packing and training conversion; incomplete or mixed-policy responses are rejected.
- [ ] Missing tensors, failed chunks and worker timeouts block generation; complete recovery re-enables it. Controlled weight/logit probes verify publication.
- [ ] Old prefix/KV state cannot be reused after a policy change; same-version reuse remains correct.
- [ ] Fresh-process resume matches continuous training state and republishes to a newly initialized engine.
- [ ] Start/close/restart, cancellation and unsupported capability checks preserve resource ownership.

Record complete source/model SHAs, dependencies, GPU placement, seeds, commands, exit codes and uncovered cases. Label evidence `CPU-MOCK`, `GPU-LOCAL`, `MULTI-RANK` or `NOT-RUN`; CPU contract checks do not replace real engine/optimizer acceptance.

Use matched hardware, precision, model, sampling, batch and update counts for performance results. Report startup separately and measure the complete rollout → reward → optimization → publication/checkpoint loop, with contention disclosed.

| Measurement | Baseline | Standard RLT backend | Speedup | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Whole training step | — | — | — | NOT-RUN |
| Rollout / training / publication | — | — | — | NOT-RUN |
| Fresh resume correctness | — | — | N/A | NOT-RUN |

Backend completion means users can select RLT through VIME's standard entry, iterate the correct recurrent policy and recover reliably, with a documented and tested support boundary.
